findings.title: Status reports "caught up: yes" when the wanted range was never evaluated
findings.description: `_product_status` sets `wanted` to `None` when `wanted_end` is unknown (lines 189-193), so `_scope` covers only the held units. Line 217 still passes `wanted=wanted_start is not None`, which is true whenever a start is configured. `caught_up` returns `all(...)` over the verdicts, and `all([])` is `True`. A product with `tier` and `start` set, no `tick_dataset_edge` row, and no units therefore gets `caught_up=True`, and `print_status` renders "caught up: yes" (`tick_status_render.py:81-87`). For a verb whose purpose is to prove completeness, this is a silent fallback. The shipped universe has `tier=None` (`universe.py:46`), so it is latent today, but it becomes reachable once an operator sets a tier and start before the first pass. Fix: pass `wanted=wanted is not None` and render the unknown-end case explicitly.

findings.title: Raw-count scan is not scoped to the shape's units or instruments
findings.description: `raw_counts` counts every `tick_trade` row in each session window for any instrument, with no `unit_id` or instrument filter. The ledger side is scoped to the shape (`_SHAPE_WHERE`, lines 55-59). `_session_row` (`tick_coverage.py:81`) builds the instrument set as the union of ledger and raw keys, so a foreign-instrument row in a session window becomes a `Mismatch` with ledger 0, and the CLI exits 3. Foreign rows are possible: ingest selects every verified tier unit when no `--unit-id` is given (`ingest_select.py:84-92`), and `_not_selectable` does not check shape for named units (`ingest_select.py:95-107`). An adopted job for another product can therefore land in `tick_trade`. The universe has one product today, so this is latent. Once a second product shares the database and the GLBX calendar, `coverage --product ES` will report false mismatches. Confidence is medium: I did not trace `adopt`'s shape acceptance end to end. Fix: restrict the raw scan to the shape's current `unit_id`s (`tick_trade` carries `unit_id`, `migrations/tick.py:244`), which mirrors the ledger definition. Add a test with a foreign-shape unit inside the window.

findings.title: Negative edge age renders as "-1d 23h"
findings.description: `age` applies chained `divmod` to `int(seconds)`. For negative input, floor division yields negative components, and `if days:` then fires. By hand, `age(-5)` and `age(-3600)` both return `-1d 23h`. The input is `now - edge.observed_at` (`tick_status_build.py:212`). `observed_at` is written with the pass process's `run.clock()` (`availability.py:150`), and status reads its own `utc_now()` (`tick_store_cmds.py:187,197`). The ingest docstring says ingest runs on a host without the Databento key, so the two hosts' clocks can differ, and a status host behind the pass host yields a negative age. No test covers `age`. Fix: refuse or clamp negative ages explicitly, and add a parametrized test that includes negative values.

findings.title: Raw scan is likely O(trades × sessions) and unmeasured
findings.description: `raw_counts` joins `tick_trade` to an `unnest` of sessions on `ts_event BETWEEN open AND close`. A range predicate cannot be hashed or merged, so the likely plan is a nested loop that compares each trade row against each session, which is O(rows × sessions). For a long range over a dense product, that is expensive. The diff has no EXPLAIN ANALYZE, and `sql.md` asks for one when tuning. I could not measure this, so the finding is unverified. Fix: measure on a realistic range first. If it is confirmed, use a per-session bounded aggregate (chunk exclusion on `ts_event`) or a LATERAL join so each trade row is touched once.

findings.title: Calendar-session helper duplicates `product_session_days`
findings.description: `calendar_sessions` builds `TradingCalendar(calendar_id, url)`, maps `psycopg.OperationalError`, `CalendarNotFoundError` and `OutOfPopulatedRangeError` to `TickCalendarError`, and closes the calendar in `finally`. `tick_calendar.product_session_days` (lines 67-81) does the same with the same three branches. The helper also lives in the status module, although `TickCalendarError` and the calendar code are in `tick_calendar.py`. Fix: move one shared function into `tick_calendar.py` and call it from both places.

findings.title: Test gaps on the wanted-range path and the new helpers
findings.description: Every new integration test uses `TICK_UNIVERSE[0]`, which has `tier=None` (`universe.py:46`). Line 87 pins `caught_up is None`. As a result, none of these run: `_wanted_end`, the wanted branch of `_scope`, `caught_up` returning True or False, `holed_sessions`, or tier rendering. A single test with a tier and start would have caught the first finding. Also untested: `age()` (no test imports it), the cross-shape exclusion in `raw_counts` (`test_tick_status_reads.py:117-132` uses one unit), and the no-contracts branch of `_product_lines`. Fix: add a parametrized case with a configured tier and start, covering no edge and no units.

findings.title: Unannotated SQL fragments may fail strict pyright
findings.description: `_UNITS`, `_LEDGER_UNITS` and `_SHAPE_WHERE` are plain module-level strings, so pyright infers `str`. They are interpolated into `conn.execute(f"...")` at lines 84-85, 101-103 and 133-138. Every sibling module annotates this kind of fragment as `LiteralString` (`manifest_reads.py:84-91`, `ingest_select.py:63`, `manifest_repo.py:163`), which is what lets pyright check psycopg's `LiteralString` query argument. Strict pyright is a merge blocker in this project. I could not run pyright, and I did not confirm the installed psycopg signature, so treat this as likely rather than confirmed. Fix: annotate the three constants `LiteralString`.

findings.title: Connection typed as `Any` at the CLI boundary
findings.description: `_read` takes `Callable[[Any, str], ...]`, and the nested `read` in `tick_coverage` takes `conn: Any` (line 228). The `Conn` alias already exists (`manifest_reads.py:29`), and `connect_migrated` returns that type. Using the alias would keep the connection typed end to end.

findings.title: F-string SQL composition
findings.description: `sql.md` says never to use f-string SQL. Here the f-strings compose only module constants and `COVERAGE_PREDICATE`, and every value goes through `%(...)s` parameters, so there is no injection path. Sibling modules do the same (`manifest_reads.py:124`). I am noting it so the exception is deliberate. The typing fix in the previous finding keeps it aligned with the project's convention.

findings.title: Repeated logging-patch block across three test files
findings.description: The `setup_logging` patch and its explanatory comment appear in `test_tick_ingest_cli.py` (the `no_key` fixture), `test_data_tick_ingest.py` (the `settings` fixture), and here as `_app_patches`. The pattern is used across roughly 40 test files, so it follows convention. A shared fixture would remove the copies.

findings.title: Contract filter re-derives the spread set by membership
findings.description: `spreads` is computed with the predicate `c.instrument_class == SPREAD_CLASS` (line 198). The contracts filter then re-derives the same set with `c not in spreads` (line 224). That is two paths to one predicate, and membership compares dataclasses by equality. Fix: filter on the predicate directly.

findings.title: `_product_lines` mutates the last bucket row and is about 53 lines
findings.description: `lines[-1] += ...` appends the degraded count to whichever row came last. That works only because the second `_BUCKET_ROWS` row is last. The function is about 53 lines, slightly over the ~50-line guideline. Both are small, but a split would make the coupling explicit.

findings.title: Exit-code mapping for status and coverage is correct
findings.description: `run_mapped` checks the `storage` tuple before `exit_code_for`, so `TickDatabaseUnreachable` maps to 4 for status and coverage. `TickPreflightError` raised from `_entries` maps to 1, because `run_context` re-exports the `store_context` class and `tick_exit.exit_code_for` imports that same class. `TickCalendarError` maps to 4 (`tick_exit.py:54-57`). Writers still see `TickDatabaseUnreachable` as a `TickPreflightError` subclass, so their exit 1 is unchanged. `test_tick_status_cli.py:142-153` covers these branches. I did not run them.

findings.title: Test DELETEs target only the fixture-created database
findings.description: `migrated_tick_db` is built on `ephemeral_tick_db` (`test/conftest.py:313`), which the conftest documents as a throwaway database owned by the test admin, the same as `ephemeral_db`. That fixture creates and drops its database (`test/conftest.py:201-226`). The DELETEs in `test_a_coverage_mismatch_exits_3` (line 122) and in `test_tick_status_build.py:112` therefore touch only that database. The new tests do not read the production URL variable.

findings.title: Refactor of the session-day helpers preserves behaviour
findings.description: `session_days` now filters `days_touched` to `[start, end)`, which matches the old loop's per-day check. No `_utc_midnight` references remain. `ingest_plan.py` no longer uses the removed `UTC`, `datetime`, or `time` imports, and its remaining `date` and `timedelta` imports are still used (lines 84 and 95).
